title: Modus Ponens
body:
**Modus ponens** takes a [[Material Conditional]] and its antecedent to its consequent.

```
P → Q
P
-----
Q
```

```
If it is a lab course, it meets twice a week.
It is a lab course.
So it meets twice a week.
```

It is valid because the only row of the conditional's truth table where `P→Q` and `P` are both
true is the row where `Q` is true. Every derivation in [[Natural Deduction]] leans on it,
and it is the elimination rule for the conditional.

The invalid pattern that resembles it is affirming the consequent, taking `P→Q` and `Q` to `P`.
That fails because the conditional permits `Q` to be true with `P` false, which is the third
row of its table.
